result:
A title edit updates the issue row and, in the same request, rewrites that issue's document in `search_index`. A later search never reads the issues table. It reads that document, after a stack of gates that can reject the query before any row is examined.

## How the new title gets into the searchable copy

Process startup is what attaches the indexer. `register` in `src/instrumentation.ts` runs once per Node server and calls `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`. That calls `registerSearchListeners` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`, which `subscribe`s on the in-process bus in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`. One of those subscriptions is `issue.updated`.

The edit itself starts at `updateIssueAction` in `src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts`. `withAction` (`src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`) parses the body with `updateIssueSchema` (`src/schemas/issue.ts`) and resolves the actor with `requireActorFor`. The action then checks `can(actor, "issue:update", …)` and calls `updateIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`.

`updateIssue` runs in this order:

1. `assertOrgScope` (`src/lib/tenant.ts`) requires `actor.orgId === input.orgId`.
2. `findIssueById` (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`) loads the current row, scoped with `orgPredicate`.
3. `assertCan(actor, "issue:update", issueResource(before))` (`src/lib/permissions.ts`) checks the real issue, and `assertNotArchived` rejects an archived one.
4. `issueRepo.updateIssue` writes only the fields present on the input. A title change sets `title` and a new `updatedAt`, then returns the row.
5. `emit("issue.updated", …)` publishes an `EventEnvelope` from `actorEnvelope` (`orgId`, `actorId`, `occurredAt`) plus `issueId`, `projectId`, and `changedFields`. `changedFields` is the input keys other than `orgId` and `issueId`. The new title is not on the event.

`emit` waits for every subscriber with `Promise.allSettled`. The search handler ignores the payload's field list. It calls `findIssueById` again and, if that returns a row, `indexIssue`. The comment on `registerSearchListeners` states why: the indexer re-reads the committed row so it cannot store a write that did not land. If the re-read returns null, it leaves the index alone.

`indexIssue` calls `upsertSearchDocument` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts` with kind `"issue"`, the issue id, `projectId`, and content `[issue.title, issue.description ?? ""].join("\n")`. The upsert looks up the existing document by `(orgId, subjectKind, subjectId)` via `orgPredicate`. If one exists it overwrites `content`, `projectId`, and `indexedAt`. Otherwise it inserts a new id from `newId()`. By the time `updateIssue` returns, the document already contains the new title. The colleague's later search is a separate request against that row.

A failed indexer does not fail the edit. `emit` reports a rejected handler to its error sinks and does not rethrow, so the issues row can commit while `search_index` stays stale.

The same listeners cover the other ordinary writes that change what search should see: `issue.created` indexes, `issue.archived` calls `removeFromIndex` → `deleteSearchDocument`, `comment.created` / `comment.deleted` and `project.created` / `project.archived` do the same for those kinds. `updateComment` writes the comment and emits nothing, so a comment edit does not refresh its document. `issue.status_changed` and `issue.assigned` are also unsubscribed; those writes do not change the indexed text. A title edit goes through `issue.updated`, which does.

`runSearchReindexJob` (`src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts`) is a separate per-org rebuild: it pages projects, issues, and comments and calls `indexProject`, `indexIssue`, and `indexComment`. The scheduler in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` enqueues `"search-reindex"` on a 1440-minute cadence with an empty payload, and the queue handler in `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` returns immediately unless `payload.orgId` is a string. Nothing in the app emits `search.reindex_requested` either. The listener for that event only reindexes when `subjectKind === "issue"`. A title edit does not wait on any of that.

## What the copy stores

The table is `searchIndex` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts` (created in `src/server/db/migrate.ts`). Each document has:

- `id`, a fresh ULID, not the subject's id
- `orgId`
- `subjectKind`: `"issue"`, `"comment"`, or `"project"`
- `subjectId`
- `projectId` (the issue's project, the project's own id, or null for a comment)
- `content`
- `indexedAt`, an ISO timestamp

For an issue, `content` is the title, a newline, and the description or `""`. Status, priority, assignee, labels, and the issue number are not stored. There is a secondary index on `(org_id, subject_kind)` only. Matching is a SQL `LIKE` over `content`, not a token index.

## What a query goes through

Three callers share `search` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`.

The search page, `Page` in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx`, loads the tenant, evaluates `advanced_search` with `isEnabled` and `buildFlagContext`, and skips the lookup when `q` is empty. Otherwise it `safeParse`s `searchQuerySchema` (`src/schemas/search.ts`): `q` must be 1–200 characters, `kinds` is `["issue"]` unless the flag is on, in which case it is `["issue", "comment", "project"]`, and `limit` is 30. It then calls `search`.

The command palette dialog (`src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx`) debounces the input and runs `parseSearchQuery` (`src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts`) before `searchAction` (`src/actions/search/search.ts`). With the flag on, `kind:` / `in:` and `project:` are pulled out into `kinds` and `projectId`, and any other `field:value` token is recorded as unknown and omitted from the text. With the flag off, the whole string stays as free text and `kinds` stays `["issue"]`. `withAction` parses `searchQuerySchema` and resolves the actor. The action then requires `can(actor, "org:read", …)`, reloads the org, and if `advanced_search` is off filters `kinds` down to `"issue"`. It calls `search` and returns only `page.items`.

`GET` in `src/app/api/search/route.ts` requires `orgSlug` and `q`, loads the actor with `getActor`, checks `org:read`, and refuses when `command_palette` is off. That flag's strategy is `{ kind: "on" }`, so the check currently passes. It parses the same schema with `limit` 10 and kinds chosen the same way, then calls `search`.

`search` then runs, in order:

1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)`.
2. `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", orgResource(input.orgId))`. Comment and project hits use this same permission.
3. `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "search:query")` (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`). The bucket's base shape is capacity 120 and 60 tokens refilled per minute, scaled by the org plan's `apiRequestsPerHour`. A denied verdict throws `Search rate limit reached; try again after ${resetAt}`.
4. `findOrgById`, then `isEnabled("advanced_search", …)` with the org's plan, the actor's role, and `settings.enabledFlagOverrides`. The flag is defined in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` as plan-gated at `enterprise` and overridable. `isEnabled` (`src/lib/feature-flags.ts`) returns true when the override list contains it, otherwise when `planAtLeast` says the plan is enterprise.
5. If `input.q` contains `:` and the flag is off, it throws `Field-scoped search is not included in this plan`.
6. `searchDocuments` filters with `orgPredicate`, `like(content, `%${q}%)`, an optional `inArray` on `subjectKind` (an empty `kinds` list adds no kind filter), and an optional `projectId` equality. It counts the matches, then loads a descending keyset page on `(indexedAt, id)` via `keysetPredicate`, `probeLimit`, and `toPage` (`src/server/repositories/_paging.ts`). A bad cursor is ignored and the first page is returned.
7. Each row becomes a `SearchHit`: `kind` and `id` from the document, `title` from the first line of `content`, `snippet` from `snippetAround` (60 characters on either side of a case-insensitive match, ellipsis if clipped), and `href` from `hrefFor` (`/issues/${id}`, `/comments/${id}`, or `/projects/${id}`).

`search` does not parse field syntax. `LIKE` treats the whole `q` as a substring, so `%` and `_` in the query are wildcards. The only field interpretation is the dialog's `parseSearchQuery`, which rewrites the payload before `searchAction`.

## When a valid-looking query is refused

`searchQuerySchema` already rejects an empty string and anything over 200 characters. Past that, three checks refuse a query the schema accepts.

The one that rejects ordinary title text is the colon check inside `search`. `advanced_search` is an enterprise feature (`minPlan: "enterprise"` in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`, also listed only on the enterprise entry of `PLAN_LIMITS`). On any other plan, unless the org's `enabledFlagOverrides` includes `advanced_search`, any `q` that contains `:` throws before `searchDocuments`. The string is otherwise legal, and a title such as `API: redesign` is stored verbatim in `content`, so the same string would match the `LIKE`. The service comment says this is deliberate: a colon is treated as field-scoped syntax and refused, rather than searched as literal text. `parseSearchQuery` does the opposite when the flag is off — it keeps the colon in the free-text remainder "so a colon in a title still finds the title" — and `SearchDialog` sends that remainder as `q`. `searchAction` and the search page also forward `q` unchanged. The refusal happens in `search`, after those callers have accepted the string. On the page there is no catch, so the throw leaves the render. The action maps it through `toActionResult`; the dialog treats a failed result as no hits.

The rate-limit check refuses the same way for any well-formed `q`, including one with no colon, once the org's `search:query` bucket cannot pay for another token.

`assertOrgScope` and `assertCan(..., "issue:read", ...)` refuse before the bucket and the flag check when the actor's org does not match `input.orgId`, or when `explain` in `src/lib/permissions.ts` denies `issue:read`. The action and the API route can refuse still earlier with `org:read`. Narrowing `kinds` to `"issue"` when the flag is off is not a refusal; the query still runs, only against issue documents.
